question.en: Called thousands of times under load, why can this method fail?

options: HttpClient is not safe on async methods
Closed sockets pile up and exhaust ports
The using block cancels the request early
answer: Closed sockets pile up and exhaust ports

explanation.en: Each disposed client leaves its connections in TIME_WAIT, so ports run out. Reuse one HttpClient (with SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime) or inject it via IHttpClientFactory.

codeSnippet:
var http = new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2) };
await http.GetAsync(slowUrl);  // server takes 10 s

question.en: What exception does the await throw once the timeout elapses?

explanation.en: HttpClient.Timeout (default 100 s) surfaces as a TaskCanceledException whose InnerException is a TimeoutException, which tells it apart from cancelling your own CancellationToken.

question.en: What does the await on the last line wait for?

options: The first UDP datagram on port 5000
A DNS lookup of the local host name
The server to bind port 5000 again
An incoming TCP connection on port 5000
answer: An incoming TCP connection on port 5000

explanation.en: Start() begins listening on every interface; AcceptTcpClientAsync completes when a client finishes the handshake and returns a TcpClient for that connection.

codeSnippet:
using var udp = new UdpClient();
int sent = await udp.SendAsync(data, new IPEndPoint(target, 9999));

question.en: What does a completed SendAsync here tell you?

options: The datagram was handed to the OS stack
Port 9999 is open on the target host
The datagram arrived in the right order
answer: The datagram was handed to the OS stack

explanation.en: UDP has no acknowledgements, so SendAsync returns the byte count queued for sending even when nobody is listening. Delivery checks must live in your own protocol.
It returns every address the name resolves to, for example ::1 and 127.0.0.1 for localhost, so code should not assume a single IPv4 result.

question.en: How does a browser learn that this Kestrel endpoint also speaks HTTP/3?

options: A DNS SRV record that Kestrel publishes
An Alt-Svc header on HTTP/1.1 or 2 replies
The TLS certificate lists the protocol
It always tries QUIC before TCP first
answer: An Alt-Svc header on HTTP/1.1 or 2 replies

explanation.en: Kestrel adds alt-svc: h3=":5001" to TCP responses; the browser then retries over QUIC on UDP 5001. HTTP/3 also requires TLS, hence UseHttps().

question.en: A proxy blocks WebSockets. Which transport does an ASP.NET Core SignalR client try next?

explanation.en: SignalR negotiates in order WebSockets, Server-Sent Events, then Long Polling, falling back automatically while keeping the same hub API.

question.en: Why can't browser JavaScript call an ASP.NET Core gRPC service without gRPC-Web?

options: gRPC only listens on raw UDP ports

explanation.en: gRPC sends its status in HTTP/2 trailers and relies on frame-level control that browser APIs do not expose. app.UseGrpcWeb() re-encodes calls so browsers can make them.
IPv6 addresses contain colons, so IPEndPoint wraps them in brackets before the port. An IPv4 endpoint prints plainly, e.g. 192.168.1.10:8080.

codeSnippet:
int n = await socket.ReceiveAsync(buffer, SocketFlags.None);
if (n == 0) { ... }

question.en: On a connected TCP socket, what does n == 0 mean?

options: The peer closed its side of the connection
No data has arrived yet; call it again
The buffer passed in was too small
The receive timed out with no bytes
answer: The peer closed its side of the connection

explanation.en: ReceiveAsync waits until data arrives; returning 0 bytes signals a graceful shutdown (FIN) by the remote end, so the loop should stop reading and close.
HttpStatusCode is an enum: casting to int gives the numeric code 201, while formatting the value itself prints its member name.

codeSnippet:
var user = await http.GetFromJsonAsync<User>("users/42");
// server replies 404 Not Found

question.en: What happens when the server returns 404?

options: It returns an empty User object

explanation.en: GetFromJsonAsync calls EnsureSuccessStatusCode before deserializing, so any non-2xx status throws HttpRequestException with StatusCode set to NotFound.
